titleText.es: La buena noticia es que, según el último informe del IPCC, si aprobamos límites agresivos para las emisiones ahora mismo, podemos limitar el calentamiento a 2°. Eso es solo MEDIA unidad de edad de hielo, lo cual no es para tanto.
titleText.en: The good news is that according to the latest IPCC report, if we enact aggressive emissions limits now, we could hold the warming to 2°C. That's only HALF an ice age unit, which is probably no big deal.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish and official English title attributes are preserved exactly. The source uses a deliberately invented UEH scale; all temperatures, scale positions, years, depths, and sea-level magnitudes are audited as excluded measurements or numbers. OCR lost several accents, fused EN LOS and DE HIELO, split ÚLTIMA and ESTADO, and omitted the large zero and question mark.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ponemos is the present form of poner for nosotros. With límites it means setting or imposing limits.

example.en: We set clear limits on the project.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: For a policy or limit, agresivo can mean forceful or stringent rather than physically violent.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: on; to (introducing what a limit applies to)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: A can introduce the activity or quantity constrained by a limit.

example.es: El país puso límites a las emisiones.
example.en: The country put limits on emissions.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Calentado is the completed-action form of calentar used after haber.

example.es: El sol habrá calentado el agua.
example.en: The sun will have warmed the water.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Frío is the masculine singular temperature adjective. After más with a definite comparison it can mean ‘coldest.’

example.es: Enero fue el mes más frío.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here norma means the reference level treated as normal, not a rule that tells people what to do.

example.es: La temperatura está por debajo de la norma.
example.en: The temperature is below the norm.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Llamemos is the nosotros command form of llamar used to propose a shared name or label.

example.es: Llamemos unidad solar a esta cantidad.
example.en: Let's call this quantity a solar unit.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: A unidad can be an agreed amount used to measure and compare other amounts.

example.es: El metro es una unidad de longitud.
example.en: The metre is a unit of length.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; introduces what receives a name
cardDefinitions.noteEn: With llamar, a can introduce the person or thing that is assigned the stated name.
This is a condition or situation, not a political state.

example.es: Comprobamos el estado actual del sistema.
example.en: We check the current state of the system.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish actual means current, not usually English ‘actual.’
As a noun, invernadero is a structure kept warm for plants. It can also evoke extremely warm climate conditions.
Cretácico names the geological period roughly 145 to 66 million years ago.

example.es: El clima cretácico era muy cálido.
example.en: The Cretaceous climate was very warm.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Subida can name an upward movement or an increase in a measured level.

example.es: La subida del nivel fue rápida.
example.en: The rise in the level was rapid.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Here polos means the geographic North and South Poles, not rods, magnets, or clothing.

example.es: Los polos reciben poca luz en invierno.
example.en: The poles receive little light in winter.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you assign a proposed name to a person or thing?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use a form of llamar, state the name, and introduce the thing receiving it with a.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The name comes directly after llamar. The a-phrase identifies what receives that label; in English the same relation is often expressed with ‘call’ and no separate equivalent of a.

example.es: Llamamos zona segura a este espacio.
example.en: We call this space a safe zone.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say ‘sea level’ in Spanish?
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Del combines de and el. The expression names the reference height of the sea's surface and is common in geography and climate discussions.

example.es: La ciudad está cerca del nivel del mar.
example.en: The city is near sea level.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: a made-up ice-age unit that makes projected warming visually comparable with major past climate change
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The chart defines one unit as the roughly 4.5-degree global difference between the coldest part of the last ice age and a modern reference. It then places projected warming on that scale. This exposes how a few degrees of global average warming can represent a climate shift comparable in magnitude to moving out of an ice age, with radically different coastlines and polar conditions.

Agresivos follows límites and describes the kind of limits.
Agresivos takes masculine plural form to agree with límites.
A finales de marks the late part of the century named after it.
Habrá is the future helper, and calentado is the completed-action form.
De media marks the following figure as an average rather than every local temperature.
Entre opens the range and y joins its two excluded measured endpoints.

applications.explanationEn: El and más mark the superlative, while the de-phrase supplies the range in which that moment is coldest.
Última comes before edad and takes the feminine singular ending that matches that noun.
Media follows temperatura and classifies it as the average temperature.
Media is feminine singular to agree with temperatura.
Más gives the greater degree of fría, and que introduces the comparison baseline.
